title: Dementia: type, stage and behavior
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cognitive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for cognitive status.

HPI
The patient is an 81-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up of his Alzheimer's disease. He is accompanied by his daughter, who reports that he remains stable at home. He continues to have some difficulty with complex tasks and short-term memory, but his daughter notes he is still able to perform basic activities of daily living with some assistance. He is currently experiencing a mild stage of cognitive decline. No behavioral changes have been reported by the family during this interval.

Medication List
Donepezil 10mg daily.

Exam
The patient is an 81-year-old male who appears well-groomed and is dressed appropriately for the weather. He is calm and cooperative throughout the encounter. He is alert and oriented to person and place. Speech is clear and coherent. His mood is stable. Cognitive testing shows he remains in a mild dementia category.

Assessment
1. Alzheimer's disease, mild stage.

Plan
1. Continue current medication regimen.
2. Follow up in three months for continued monitoring of cognitive function.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Alzheimer's disease: G30.9, sequenced first; the dementia is then coded with F02.- (dementia in other diseases classified elsewhere).
Alzheimer's disease (F02.-, dementia in other diseases), mild, without behavioral disturbance: F02.A0.

distractors.why: F02.- is a manifestation code: code first the underlying Alzheimer's disease (G30.9).
The provider documents the stage (mild): it decides the code and the HCC.
Dementia due to Alzheimer's disease is F02.- (in other diseases), not F03.- (unspecified dementia).
